gradingDesign.rule: All variable student evidence is graded only in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes distance from displacement in the City Blocks Challenge?
In Level 2, a successful route has a distance of 8 blocks and returns to its starting point. If it takes 8 minutes, what is its average speed in blocks per minute?
Level 4 requires a distance of 6 blocks and an average speed of 0.75 block/min. How many total minutes must the route take?
Every moved block takes one minute. If the successful Level 4 route moves 6 blocks but must last 8 minutes, how many WAIT moves are required?
Level 5 requires a distance of 8 blocks and an average speed of 0.80 block/min. How many total minutes must the route take?
Level 6 requires a displacement magnitude of 4 blocks and an average velocity magnitude of 0.50 block/min. How many total minutes must the route take?
What does pressing WAIT do to average speed when distance stays unchanged?
A traveler moves 3 blocks east and then 3 blocks west, ending at the starting point. Which result is correct?
Use one completed City Blocks route to show how its distance, displacement, and total time determine its average speed or average velocity. Include the route values and calculation.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Cite values visible in your completed route and use the matching rate equation.
a. Full credit: Gives distance or displacement, total time, the correct division, a correct rate with units, and identifies whether the result is average speed or average velocity.
  Partial credit: Uses the correct relationship but omits one route value, unit, or label, or makes a minor arithmetic error.
  No credit: Uses unrelated values, divides in the wrong order without correction, or provides no calculation.

questions.prompt: Compare the strategy you used on one distance-and-displacement level with the strategy you used on a rate level. Explain how backtracking and WAIT moves affect distance, displacement, time, average speed, and average velocity.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Use evidence from at least two completed levels and distinguish route length, position change, and elapsed time.
a. Full credit: Cites two levels, accurately explains how backtracking can increase distance without the same increase in displacement, explains how WAIT increases time without changing distance or displacement, and connects both effects to the rate calculations.
  Partial credit: Gives a generally correct strategy comparison but omits one level, one quantity, or a clear connection to a rate.
  No credit: Treats distance and displacement as identical, says WAIT changes position, or gives no completed-level evidence.
